meta.title: Bedug · Prayer times, Quran, Qibla and Hijri calendar
meta.description: Bedug is a free prayer-times app with reminders, the Quran, dzikir and duas, a Hijri calendar, Ramadan countdowns, a zakat calculator and a Qibla compass. Private, offline and at home on iOS, Android, macOS, Windows and Linux.

mock.label: Bedug showing today's prayer times in {place}, with {next} up next

hero.title: The mosque drum, in your pocket.
hero.lead: Before the adhan, mosques across Indonesia beat the bedug. This app does the same job: it tells you when the next prayer is, wherever you are, and keeps the Quran, dzikir and the Qibla close for the time in between.
hero.note: Free on iPhone, iPad, Android, Mac, Windows and Linux. No ads, no account, and it works offline.

showcase.alt: The Quran reader showing the first page of Al-Baqara
showcase.title: The Quran, laid out like the mushaf
showcase.body: Page mode follows the 604 pages of the Madinah mushaf, and a page turns like paper under your finger. Or read ayah by ayah with a translation, bookmark where you stop, and let the khatam planner split what's left into daily portions by juz.

showcase.alt: A morning dzikir card with Ayat al-Kursi, its transliteration and a count of one
showcase.title: Dzikir with the count on the card
showcase.body: Morning and evening dzikir from Hisnul Muslim, Al-Ma'thurat or Ratib Siribee, with the Arabic, a transliteration and a translation. Tap the card for each recitation, and long-press to start again.

showcase.alt: The Qibla compass in Jakarta, pointing 295 degrees, 7,920 km from the Kaaba
showcase.title: The Qibla, with or without a compass
showcase.body: On a phone, turn until the Kaaba sits at the top of the dial. A computer has no compass, so Bedug gives the bearing, the distance to Makkah and where the Qibla lies from the sun.

showcase.alt: The Ramadan fasting log with 8 of 29 days fasted and 2 fasts to make up
showcase.title: A fasting log that keeps count of qada
showcase.body: Mark each day of Ramadan as fasted, missed or excused. The days you owe carry over from year to year until you make them up. Around it: a sahur alarm, countdowns to imsak and iftar, and reminders the evening before Monday and Thursday fasts, the White Days, Arafah and Ashura.

more.title: Prayer times
more.body: Kemenag RI by default, or one of nine other methods such as Muslim World League, ISNA and Umm al-Qura, with Shafi'i or Hanafi Asr. Imsak, sunrise, Dhuha and the last third of the night too.

more.title: Reminders and widgets
more.body: A notification for each prayer, early if you like, with the bedug drum or a tone from your phone. Home screen widgets for the next prayer, the ayah of the day and Ramadan.

more.title: Hijri calendar
more.body: Umm al-Qura or MABIMS, adjustable by up to two days, with Islamic holidays and a reminder at Maghrib the evening before.

more.title: Duas and Asmaul Husna
more.body: Dzikir after prayer, daily duas for waking, eating and travel, and the 99 names of Allah.

more.title: Zakat
more.body: Zakat maal against the gold nisab, and zakat fitrah for your household. What you own is never saved.

more.title: Location
more.body: Use GPS, or pick your city and leave location off. You always see a city name, never coordinates.

more.title: Languages
more.body: Indonesian, English, Arabic and Malay, with a full right-to-left layout in Arabic.

more.title: Made for each platform
more.body: Liquid Glass on iPhone and Mac, Material You on Android, Fluent on Windows, and Adwaita or Breeze on Linux.

infaq.title: No ads, no account, no server
infaq.body: Prayer times are calculated on your device. Your bookmarks, reading position and fasting log stay on it, and this website sets no cookies. Bedug is paid for by infaq from the people who use it, and every infaq goes to its development, not to a charity or anyone else.
infaq.in_app: In the Android and Apple apps, give an infaq from Settings through Google Play or the App Store. On Windows and Linux, use the links here.
infaq.links_soon: The infaq links open with the first release.

privacy.meta_description: How Bedug handles your data: prayer times are calculated on your device, there is no account, and your settings stay with you.
privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: Bedug is a prayer-times app published by Ardeman. This policy explains what data the app and this website use, and why. Bedug has no account and no server of its own, so your data stays on your device.
summary: No account, no sign-up, no Bedug server.
Your location is used on your device to calculate prayer times and the Qibla.
Your settings, bookmarks, reading progress and fasting log are stored only on your device.
Bedug shows no ads and has no ad or analytics SDK.
This website uses no cookies and no analytics.

sections.heading: Data the app uses
body: Location. With auto detect on, Bedug asks your device for its location to calculate prayer times and the Qibla direction. The coordinates are used on your device and are not sent to us. To show your city's name, Bedug uses your device's built-in geocoding service, which sends the coordinates to Apple (on iOS and macOS) or Google (on Android); see the Apple and Google privacy policies. If you turn auto detect off and pick a city, Bedug doesn't use your location.
Compass. The Qibla compass reads your device's heading sensor. The reading is used on your device only.

Settings and your worship data. Your calculation method, city, language, theme and notification choices, your Quran bookmarks, last-read position and khatam plan, and your fasting log are stored on your device and are deleted when you uninstall the app. The zakat calculator saves only the gold price and the fitrah amount you enter; what you own is never stored.
Notifications. Prayer, dzikir, fasting and Hijri event reminders are scheduled on your device. No server sends them.
Home screen widgets. The app passes the coming days' prayer times and ayahs to its widgets on your device. They stay on your device.

sections.heading: Infaq
body: In the Android and Apple apps, an infaq is an in-app purchase handled by Google Play or the App Store. We don't receive your payment details. The app only learns whether the purchase succeeded and stores that on your device to thank you.
An infaq through Trakteer or Ko-fi is handled by that service under its own privacy policy. It shares with us only what you choose to give, such as a name and a message.

sections.heading: This website
body: bedug.ardeman.com uses no cookies, no analytics and no third-party scripts, and serves its fonts itself. It is hosted on Cloudflare, and Cloudflare processes your IP address and request details to deliver and protect the site; see the Cloudflare privacy policy.

To preview prayer times on the home page, the site uses the approximate location (city, coordinates and time zone) that Cloudflare estimates from your IP address. Your browser calculates the times from it, and it is not stored or sent anywhere else.

sections.heading: Children
body: Bedug is not directed at children under 13, and we don't knowingly collect data from them.

sections.heading: Your choices
body: You can turn location off and pick a city instead, turn notifications off, and remove all of Bedug's data by uninstalling the app. We keep no data about you on any server, so there is nothing for us to export or delete.

sections.heading: Changes
body: If this policy changes, we'll update this page and the effective date at the top.

sections.heading: Contact
body: Questions about this policy? Open an issue on GitHub.
